goal: Adds benchmarks for TxIndex, TxoSpenderIndex and BlockFilterIndex sync and lookup, so index changes can be measured without a full IBD.
Lets contributors compare disk vs memory sync cost and per-key lookup cost for these three indexes.

result.summary: Adds shared helpers and three new benchmark suites (TxIndex, TxoSpenderIndex, BlockFilterIndex) that build a chain of blocks with realistic chained, multi-input/output transactions, then measure full sync (disk vs memory) and per-key lookup cost. It also documents, in doc/benchmarking.md, how to measure syscalls, on-disk size, and peak memory around bench_bitcoin since the framework itself does not report those. The existing coinbase-only BlockFilterIndexSync benchmark is left untouched.
result.problem: There was no cheap way to tell whether a change to txindex, txospenderindex, or blockfilterindex actually helps, short of a full IBD; the one existing index benchmark only syncs coinbase-only blocks and cannot show anything that scales with block contents. Contributors working on index performance (e.g. the authors of #35531 and #34489) feel this most directly.

open_concerns: arejula27 asked how to interpret TxoSpenderIndex::FindSpender's util::Expected<optional,...> return type; l0rinc has not answered.
Minor question about whether two conditions in index_txospender.cpp are identical was raised by l0rinc; no explicit reply visible in the diff, though later force-pushes may have addressed it.
resolved_concerns: l0rinc's nit to use 1_MiB literal was applied (util/byte_units.h now included).
l0rinc's concern about arch-dependent types and locking inside the measured block appear addressed by later force-pushes (author's own comment 'mb' and subsequent restructuring).

The benchmarks initially measured the wrong thing because the default tmpfs data directory hid the disk/memory distinction and because chainstate was never flushed so BaseIndex::Commit() short-circuited; both were found and fixed by the author, who documented the tmpfs caveat and added an explicit flush.

result.card: This PR adds reusable benchmark infrastructure for TxIndex, TxoSpenderIndex, and BlockFilterIndex, building realistic chains of chained transactions to measure full sync (disk vs memory) and per-key lookup cost, plus a documentation section on measuring I/O and memory around bench_bitcoin. The problem is that there was previously no cheap way to evaluate index performance changes short of a full IBD, and the only existing benchmark used coinbase-only blocks that could not scale with block contents. The strongest evidence of value is the author's own use of these benchmarks to produce concrete numbers for two other open index PRs, #35531 and #34489. Review state is Ready: the sole reviewer (l0rinc) gave a concept ACK plus nits, most of which the first-time contributor author has addressed across several force pushes, including fixing a real bug where the benchmarks never reached the commit path. Agreement is Positive with no standing objection to the change itself, though one clarifying question about an index API's return type remains unanswered.
